Topic: Introduction to Electrical Safety and Tools
LearningOutcomes: Students will identify electrical hazards, apply safety precautions, and correctly use common electrical installation tools.
LectureTopics: Overview of electrical hazards and risk assessment
Personal protective equipment (PPE) for electricians
Introduction to common hand and power tools used in electrical installation
Zambian electrical safety regulations and standards overview
AssessmentMethods: Practical tool identification quiz and safety checklist completion
FeedbackComments: Well-structured introduction. Ensure students handle all tools during the practical session.

LearningOutcomes: Students will understand and construct simple series and parallel circuits, interpreting basic wiring diagrams.
LectureTopics: Series and parallel circuit theory
Reading and interpreting basic wiring diagrams
Practical wiring of a single-phase circuit
Testing and verifying circuit continuity using a multimeter
AssessmentMethods: Practical wiring exercise graded on accuracy and safety compliance
FeedbackComments: Good progression from Week 1. Allocate extra time for students struggling with multimeter use.

LearningOutcomes: Students will demonstrate proper welding safety practices and identify the main components of arc welding equipment.
LectureTopics: Welding hazards: fumes, arc flash, fire, and electric shock
Personal protective equipment for welding
Components of a SMAW (arc welding) setup
Workshop housekeeping and fire prevention
AssessmentMethods: Safety quiz and equipment identification practical assessment
FeedbackComments: Comprehensive safety coverage. Consider adding a fire drill scenario.

LearningOutcomes: Students will explain the communication process, identify barriers to effective communication, and apply basic principles of professional workplace communication.
LectureTopics: The communication process: sender, message, channel, receiver
Verbal and non-verbal communication in the workplace
Barriers to effective communication and strategies to overcome them
Introduction to professional writing: emails and memos

Materials.Title: Communication Skills in the Workplace Reference

AssessmentMethods: In-class participation and short reflective writing exercise on communication barriers
FeedbackComments: Well-planned introduction. Ensure the writing exercise reflects real workplace scenarios.

LearningOutcomes: Students will identify the main hardware components of a desktop computer, describe their functions, and perform basic assembly and disassembly procedures.
LectureTopics: Overview of computer history and types of computers
Internal hardware components: CPU, RAM, motherboard, storage devices
External peripherals: input and output devices
Practical: identifying and labelling computer components
AssessmentMethods: Practical component identification exercise and short written quiz
